data.turoyo: <...> ‘Taʕlo, lṭaš ʕarši d̥qoṭanno i+ʕezo+koviye. Ono ŭ hat gduxlina u+baṣrayḏa’.
data.translation: <...> ‘Fox, sharpen my tooth so that I’ll kill the wild goat. You and I’ll eat her meat’.

rationale: First Imperativ box; explicit addressee, tooth object and purpose.

data.turoyo: Xori Brahim: W kəḥliwo ʕaynayye, əmmiwo (gaḥxo) hayo kətwo, saymiwo, əmmiwo "u kuḥlo kayiso yo" w ləbxiwo ʕayne dan naʕime, mənayye mlaṭšiwonne kulle daqqat, hawxa saymiwonne. Kətwo kəḥliwo ʕaynayye ste šafiro, buwwe.
data.translation: Khori Brahim: And they used to paint their eyes with kohl, they used to say (laughing), that existed, they did it, they used to say, 'The kohl is good,' and they would hold the children's eyes and dab some of it on them, all dots; that is what they did to them. There were people who also painted their eyes properly with it.

rationale: Only attestation of provisional new II stem and Infectum-wa box, with kohl/eye context.

summary: The inherited single sense combines sharpening and soaping/cleaning. Preserve it exactly; sparse-cell examples now distinguish the applications without renumbering old material.
Imperativ lṭaš is securely attested with an overt fox addressee and tooth object. The unrelated quadriliteral smear verb need not be recruited.
The explicit feminine ela and -la agree in the horn-sharpening Preterit. lṭišole at 103/35 contains feminine object coding; the German modal intention does not establish a different form box.
At MAC NE Shangali Pangali/13 the source sound sequence may indicate grinding manner. Withhold a new noise sense, idiom or uncertain example.
No new light-verb collocation is established.
The Jan m-prefixed mlaṭšiwonne cannot be put into the already-proposed I Imperativ box or identified from German sharpening glosses. It provisionally establishes II Infectum-wa.
The matter applied is resumed by mənayye; eyes are the affected surface/object, and kulle daqqat describes dots. The verb is not a light-verb expression.
The source supports lexical dabbing/smearing in a cosmetic setting, not a distinct specialised technical sense. Existing I wording and all round-1 proposals remain intact.
Is singular ʕarši literally one tooth or collective teeth in MAC NE Shangali Pangali/12?
At /13, are xәruǧәnák̇ xәrxәronák̇ grinding noises, a manner expression or an implement name? Who or how many are the agents of lṭəšše?
At 103/35, is the vowel in lṭišole conditioned by object coding, and does the temporal clause have an intended/prospective interpretation?
Should sharpening and soaping eventually be split editorially? Existing sense 1 is retained in full.
Confirm II/root filing of mlaṭšiwonne and obtain its native Preterit/Infectum bases; only the Infectum-wa shape is attested here. Is dabbing in dots inherent to the verb or supplied by kulle daqqat?
Sharpened objects now include horn, tooth and razor beside the inherited sword; the source preserves explicit body-part possessors and feminine object agreement.
